newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesian rupiah stable, shrugs off Suharto rumour.
newsitem.headline: Indonesian rupiah stable, shrugs off Suharto rumour.

text.p: The Indonesian rupiah was stable against the dollar in slow late trading on Tuesday as players shrugged off unfounded rumours that President Suharto had gone to hospital for treatment, dealers said.
"Operators did not rush to buy dollars and sell rupiah. The rumour appeared to be weak," a dealer with a large privately-owned local bank said.
Suharto on Tuesday visited retired general Abdul Haris Nasution in a Jakarta military hospital where he was recuperating from minor surgery, palace sources said.
The sources denied the rumour, said to be coming from Japan, in the foreign exchange market that Suharto had gone to the hospital for treatment.
Spot rupiah was generally stable as it was last quoted at 2,396.50/97.00 at 0840 GMT from 2,396.50/97.50 at the opening.
Tomorrow and today rupiah were at 2,396.50/97.00 and 2,396.50/97.00 respectively.
"I think such a rumour, unless it is very strong, will be unlikely to have much of an impact on the market in the future as we have heard similar rumours several times before," another dealer said.
Dealers said rupiah liquidity remained ample in late trading despite weekly corporate tax payments.
They said the local currency was expected to remain little changed on Wednesday, with the spot rate seen moving in a range between 2,396.50 to 2,397.50.
Overnight swap was last quoted at par/0.05 and tom/next at 0.10/0.15.
One-month swaps were last quoted at 9.75/10.50, two at 22.0/23.0, three at 35.0/36.0 and six to 75.0/76.0 points.
Bank Indonesia kept its intervention band at 2,386/2,578 and the conversion band at 2,386/2,434 late on Tuesday.
